macro.title: Escalating Iran‑US standoff spikes geopolitical risk
macro.body: Recent reports of a deepening stalemate between Tehran and Washington raise the probability of a broader Middle‑East conflict. Such an event would likely push oil prices higher and increase safe‑haven demand, benefitting energy exporters and defensive assets while pressuring risk assets globally.
macro.bull: Energy‑heavy positions like ENB.TO could rally on higher crude.
macro.base: Markets absorb the news with modest volatility, leaving most holdings unchanged.
macro.bear: Escalation could trigger a risk‑off sell‑off, hurting leveraged equity ETFs.

macro.title: US homebuilder sentiment hits 14‑year low
macro.body: The NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index fell to its weakest level since 2009, reflecting weakening demand for new construction. While the US housing sector is a small direct exposure for this portfolio, the broader sentiment can pressure consumer‑discretionary stocks and amplify volatility in the S&P 500.
macro.bull: Lower housing costs could boost consumer spending, supporting retail and tech earnings.
macro.base: Sentiment dip is largely priced in; core holdings remain stable.
macro.bear: Continued weakness may spill into broader equity markets, dragging leveraged ETFs.

macro.title: ECB signals possible rate cut in early 2027
macro.body: Eurozone policymakers hinted at a rate reduction to combat slowing growth, which could weaken the euro against the Canadian dollar. A stronger CAD would reduce the CAD value of any future USD‑denominated cash flows, but the immediate effect is limited for a non‑resident investor whose holdings are already USD‑heavy.
macro.bull: A stronger CAD improves purchasing power for future Canadian‑dollar expenses like the FHSA down‑payment.
macro.base: FX move is modest; portfolio exposure remains dominated by USD assets.
macro.bear: If the euro weakens sharply, the CAD could appreciate, eroding USD‑denominated holdings.
macro.bear_estimate: USD notional $134,447 USD * 1‑cent move = $1,344 CAD loss

risks.title: Leverage Decay Risk – 3x ETFs in Elevated Volatility
risks.context: VIX is above 22, amplifying decay in SPXL ($53,911), FNGU ($43,487) and UDOW ($18,870) – together $116,268 CAD of leveraged exposure.
risks.body: When volatility stays high, leveraged ETFs lose value each day regardless of market direction. The portfolio’s 52% allocation to 3x ETFs makes it especially vulnerable to a prolonged VIX rally.

risks.title: FX Exposure Drag – Potential CAD Strengthening
risks.context: USD holdings total $192,166 CAD (≈ $134,447 USD). A 0.01 CAD fall in USD/CAD reduces CAD value by $1,344 per cent, equating to a $13,440 CAD hit if the rate moves 0.10 lower.
risks.body: A stronger Canadian dollar would erode the CAD value of all US‑denominated positions, notably SPXL, FNGU, NVDA and other USD‑priced stocks, creating a hidden drag on returns.

risks.title: Earnings Concentration – Tech Mega‑Cap Overweight
risks.context: Tech mega‑caps (NVDA $8,899, AAPL $2,012, MSFT $1,482, TSLA $7,551, TSM $8,039) represent $28,883 CAD, ~11% of the portfolio.
risks.body: Heavy reliance on a handful of high‑growth tech names raises tail‑risk; a miss in any of their earnings could disproportionately affect portfolio performance.

news.headline: Nvidia earnings preview: AI test and market volatility
news.body: Wall Street is awaiting Nvidia’s earnings, with analysts warning that a miss could spark a broader AI‑sector sell‑off. NVDA is a core holding (non‑sell) and its movement will also influence the FNGU leveraged ETF exposure to the FANG+ index.

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: NVDA beats expectations, lifting AI sentiment and boosting FNGU.

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: NVDA posts in‑line results; modest movement in FNGU.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: NVDA misses, triggering a pullback in AI stocks and FNGU.

news.headline: Tesla commits $3.3bn to German Gigafactory expansion
news.body: Tesla announced a major capital allocation to its German plant, signalling confidence in European demand. TSLA is a holding ($7,551 CAD) and the news may lift the broader EV sector, benefitting leveraged exposure via SPXL and UDOW.
news.exposure: TSLA $7,551 CAD, SPXL $53,911 CAD, UDOW $18,870 CAD

outcomes.label: Bull
outcomes.scenario: Expansion viewed positively, EV stocks rally.
outcomes.estimate: TSLA +4% ≈ +$302 CAD; SPXL +2% ≈ +$1,078 CAD; UDOW +2% ≈ +$377 CAD

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Market digests the news with little price movement.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Cost concerns trigger a pullback in TSLA and related ETFs.
outcomes.estimate: TSLA ‑3% ≈ ‑$227 CAD; SPXL ‑2% ≈ ‑$1,078 CAD; UDOW ‑2% ≈ ‑$377 CAD

news.headline: US retail sales rise modestly in October
news.body: Retail sales grew 0.3% YoY, indicating resilient consumer spending. This supports the broader S&P 500, benefitting leveraged ETFs SPXL and UDOW, while also underpinning discretionary stocks like COST and LYV.
news.exposure: SPXL $53,911 CAD, UDOW $18,870 CAD, COST $4,763 CAD, LYV $2,795 CAD

outcomes.label: Base
outcomes.scenario: Sales data is in line with expectations; markets stay flat.

outcomes.label: Bear
outcomes.scenario: Data seen as weak, prompting a minor pullback.

picks.thesis: Shopify’s recent earnings beat and expanding merchant services franchise provide exposure to Canadian tech growth without adding to US‑denominated volatility.
picks.entry: Target entry around CAD 55–57 per share; monitor Q4 earnings and merchant volume trends.

picks.thesis: Enphase Energy benefits from the accelerating residential solar rollout and its micro‑inverter market share gains, offering a clean‑energy play complementary to ENB and SHEL.
picks.entry: Enter on pull‑back near USD 150–155; watch U.S. solar incentive policy updates.

strengths.text: Large USD exposure ($192,166 CAD) positions the portfolio to gain if the CAD weakens against the dollar.
Tax‑advantaged FHSA and RRSP holdings (e.g., TXF.TO $34,893 CAD) shelter growth from immediate taxation.
High notional exposure to the S&P 500 via SPXL ($53,911 CAD) captures broad US equity upside.
Diversified sector mix across tech, financials, energy and consumer staples reduces single‑sector dependence.
Minimal uninvested cash ($1,482 CAD total) limits idle capital drag while preserving liquidity for opportunistic buys.

concerns.text: Over‑concentration in 3x leveraged ETFs (52% of portfolio) raises volatility and decay risk.
Liquidity of leveraged ETFs can tighten during market stress, potentially widening bid‑ask spreads.
NVDA is a core holding that cannot be sold; any sharp correction would disproportionately affect the portfolio.
RRSP cash balance is only $112 CAD, limiting ability to fund new positions without pulling from other accounts.
Sector overlap between US tech mega‑caps and Canadian tech ETF TXF.TO may amplify correlation risk.

strategy_short.text: Monitor VIX levels; if VIX stays above 22 for two consecutive weeks, consider trimming 3x ETF exposure by up to 10% of each position.
Set a stop‑loss band of 8% on NVDA and TSLA to limit single‑stock tail risk while preserving upside.
Deploy the $112 CAD RRSP cash into the new ENPH position once the price pulls back to the target range.

strategy_mid.text: Rebalance the portfolio over the next 12 months to reduce leveraged ETF weight to 35% and increase dividend‑yielding Canadian stocks (e.g., BMO, RY) for stability.
Utilize the FHSA/ RRSP Home Buyers’ Plan window to allocate $15,000 CAD toward the down‑payment fund, freeing up non‑tax‑sheltered cash for future investments.
Add a modest position in a defensive utility (e.g., Fortis Inc. FTS.TO) to hedge against potential equity market pullbacks.

strategy_long.text: Gradually shift a portion of USD exposure into Canadian real assets (e.g., REITs, infrastructure) to diversify currency risk over the 5‑year horizon.
Build a core retirement base in the RRSP with low‑turnover, high‑quality dividend stocks to benefit from tax‑deferred growth until repatriation in 2027.
Plan for eventual repatriation of foreign income by establishing a CAD‑denominated cash buffer in 2027 to avoid exchange‑rate timing risk.

tax.text: Since 2026 is a non‑resident year, RRSP contributions remain tax‑deductible but withdrawals will be subject to 25% withholding; keep contributions modest and document the HBP repayment schedule to avoid penalties.

recent.name: Live Nation Entertainment, Inc.
summary: Live Nation posted Q3 2026 revenue and EPS that beat Wall Street estimates, driven by strong live‑event demand with 170 million tickets sold and nearly 180 million fans projected for the year.
The company highlighted continued robust demand for live events and reaffirmed its outlook for a high‑attendance 2026 season, but did not disclose any new quantitative guidance in the coverage.
The earnings surprise was notable, with earnings exceeding expectations by roughly 12.7%, underscoring a stronger‑than‑expected profit performance.

recent.name: QUALCOMM Incorporated
summary: Revenue of $10.32 billion in calendar Q3 2026 beat Wall Street expectations but fell 8.4% year‑over‑year.
The company projected next‑quarter revenue of $10.8 billion at the midpoint, about 2.6% above analysts’ consensus, and warned that chip‑design margins are under pressure.
Investors were surprised by the margin warning and rising semiconductor input costs, which outweighed the revenue beat.

recent.name: Energy Transfer LP
summary: Q3 revenue topped expectations while earnings per share fell short
Company raised its full‑year EBITDA outlook and highlighted strong distributable cash flow
The EPS miss was a surprise compared with the revenue beat

recent.name: Apple Inc.
summary: The earnings showed a forecast for the holiday period that topped Wall Street estimates but overall mixed results left investors disappointed.
Apple highlighted a holiday‑period outlook that exceeded expectations, indicating confidence in near‑term demand.
The main surprise was that despite beating forecasts, the results failed to impress investors, signaling concern over the mixed performance.

macro_history.title: Canada CPI Surprise Could Shift CAD Outlook
macro_history.body: Statistics Canada is set to release the November CPI today. A reading notably above the 2.1% target would pressure the Canadian dollar, reducing the CAD value of the portfolio’s large USD‑denominated holdings. Conversely, a softer print could buoy the CAD and trim the USD exposure gain.
macro_history.bull: If CPI comes in hotter, the CAD weakens and USD‑denominated assets gain.
macro_history.base: Most likely the CPI will be near consensus, leaving the CAD relatively flat.
macro_history.bear: A cooler CPI would strengthen the CAD, eroding USD asset value.

macro_history.title: US Debt‑Ceiling Standoff Raises Yield Volatility
macro_history.body: Negotiations in Washington over raising the US debt ceiling are intensifying. Prolonged deadlock could push Treasury yields higher, hurting high‑beta leveraged ETFs while benefitting short‑duration credit assets. The portfolio’s 3x equity ETFs are especially sensitive to yield spikes.
macro_history.bull: Yield rise depresses leveraged equity ETFs, creating buying opportunities at lower prices.
macro_history.base: Negotiations resolve without major disruption, yields stay stable.
macro_history.bear: A sudden default risk spikes yields, causing sharp drops in leveraged ETFs.

macro_history.title: China Export Data Signals Global Trade Re‑balancing
macro_history.body: Preliminary export figures from China showed a modest rebound, hinting at renewed demand for high‑tech components. This could lift semiconductor exposure globally, benefitting holdings like TSM and SOXL, while also supporting broader risk‑on sentiment.
macro_history.bull: Export rebound lifts semiconductor demand, boosting TSM and SOXL.
macro_history.base: Exports stay modest, limited impact on tech exposure.
macro_history.bear: Exports falter, dampening global tech demand and pressuring semiconductor stocks.

macro_history.body: Recent data shows the Canadian dollar slipping against the US dollar, driven by lower oil prices and dovish expectations from the Bank of Canada. A weaker CAD raises the CAD value of the portfolio’s large US‑denominated exposure (≈$192,166 CAD notional). This benefits the CAD‑return but also increases FX volatility risk.
macro_history.bull: If CAD falls further, USD‑based holdings gain more CAD value.
macro_history.base: Modest CAD depreciation continues, adding modest upside.
macro_history.bear: A sudden CAD rebound would erode the CAD value of USD assets.

macro_history.title: Steepening US Treasury Yield Curve Hits Leveraged Equity ETFs
macro_history.body: The 10‑year/2‑year Treasury spread widened this week as investors priced in higher long‑term rates. Higher rates increase financing costs for leveraged ETFs and can compress their returns, especially in a rising‑rate environment.
macro_history.bull: If the spread stabilises, leveraged ETFs can maintain their premium exposure.
macro_history.base: Yield curve remains volatile, likely neutralising most leveraged ETF performance.
macro_history.bear: Further steepening could trigger decay in 3x ETFs as financing costs rise.

macro_history.title: European LNG Demand Shift Hits North‑American Energy Stocks
macro_history.body: Europe’s slower transition to Asian‑sourced LNG is keeping demand for North‑American gas exports high, supporting Canadian pipeline projects and energy majors. This benefits Enbridge’s pipeline earnings and Shell’s gas production outlook.
macro_history.bull: Sustained European demand lifts ENB cash flow.
macro_history.base: Demand remains steady, providing modest support.
macro_history.bear: If Europe accelerates Asian LNG imports, North‑American gas prices could fall.

macro_history.title: Fed Rate Decision Looms as Inflation Shows Mixed Signals
macro_history.body: The Federal Reserve is expected to announce its policy decision later this month. With US CPI data still volatile, markets are split on whether rates will hold or rise again.
macro_history.base: A hold decision keeps the status quo for USD/CAD and the portfolio’s mixed exposure.

macro_history.title: Oil Prices Slip to $87/bbl Pressuring Energy Revenues
macro_history.body: U.S. crude fell to $87 a barrel as Middle‑East exports recover, tightening margins for North American energy firms. Canadian exporters and pipeline operators could see lower cash flow, affecting dividend yields and share price momentum.
macro_history.bull: If the price rebound quickly, ENB and SHEL could rally on improved cash flow.
macro_history.base: Stable oil prices keep current valuations largely unchanged.
macro_history.bear: Prolonged low oil drags energy stocks, cutting portfolio value.

macro_history.title: Saudi Military Leadership Shuffle Raises Geopolitical Uncertainty
macro_history.body: Saudi Arabia’s replacement of its top commander after a Yemen setback adds volatility to Middle‑East geopolitics. Heightened risk can spur oil price spikes, indirectly benefiting Canadian energy exporters while also increasing global market risk aversion.
macro_history.bull: A short‑term oil rally would lift ENB and SHEL valuations.
macro_history.base: Markets may price in a neutral outcome, leaving energy exposure unchanged.
macro_history.bear: Escalation could trigger broader risk‑off, hurting equity exposure across the board.

macro_history.title: US Fiscal Stimulus Bill Clears Congress
macro_history.body: Congress approved a $300 billion infrastructure and tax credit package, injecting liquidity into the US economy and supporting corporate earnings. The boost to US fiscal spending tends to lift equity markets, especially large‑cap US stocks that dominate the SPXL position.
macro_history.bull: Higher corporate profits lift the S&P 500, benefitting the 3x leveraged SPXL.
macro_history.base: Modest equity rally as stimulus expectations are priced in.
macro_history.bear: If the bill stalls in the Senate, market sentiment could turn negative, pulling US equities lower.

macro_history.title: China Manufacturing PMI Surges Above 50
macro_history.body: The official manufacturing PMI rose to 51.2 in November, indicating a rebound in Chinese factory activity. A stronger Chinese economy supports global demand for semiconductors and tech components, benefitting TSMC exposure.
macro_history.bull: Improved demand lifts TSMC earnings and its CAD‑valued position.
macro_history.bear: A slowdown after the PMI peak could pressure semiconductor orders.

macro_history.title: Canada Approves New East Coast LNG Pipeline Expansion
macro_history.body: The federal regulator gave the green light to expand the Atlantic LNG pipeline, increasing capacity for Canadian natural gas exports to Europe. Higher gas flows should benefit Enbridge's Canadian‑listed assets and broader energy exposure.
macro_history.bull: Expanded export capacity lifts Enbridge's cash flow.
macro_history.base: Pipeline approval is priced in, leaving ENB relatively unchanged.
macro_history.bear: If construction delays arise, the anticipated benefit could be deferred.
